independent.summary: The write floor is bypassable through `POST /chat`, which this change deliberately leaves ungated on the stated premise that "asking the assistant a question reads the graph and writes nothing to it" (app.js:176-180, docs/api.md, Decision Log). On the Responses-API path (any provider with `responsesApi: true` plus `MCP_SERVER_URL` set, app.js-adjacent chat.js:528) the route hands the model this deployment's own MCP server via `mcpToolDef()` with `require_approval: 'never'` and no `allowed_tools` restriction, authenticated with `MCP_BEARER_TOKEN`. The ten write tools therefore run with the role of `Settings.mcpUserId` (normally an owner/editor), not the caller's, so a viewer can say "create/rename/delete this entity" in chat and the write lands — the same hole the item identified for the direct connector, left open for chat's relay to it, and untested by the new MCP group.

The documented falsification check for the changelog rollback gate is wrong, so the behavioural sweep does not test what it claims. The swept URL is `/entities/<id>/rollback/<logId>`, which first passes the `/entities` mount (app.js:161) whose `requireWriteRole` already refuses a viewer; removing `requireWriteRole` from the rollback route in changelog.js:191 would still produce a 403 `NOT_WORKSPACE_EDITOR` in the behavioural sweep. Only the static assertion catches that regression, not "both sweeps" as the header states.

grades.reason: This change gates /mcp by exactly the mechanism the item specified — `mcpWriteWorkspaceId()` in lib/mcpWorkspace.js, wired into all ten write tools in routes/mcp.js — so a viewer connector does not keep write access.
`mcpWriteWorkspaceId` is defined in this same diff at server/src/lib/mcpWorkspace.js:64 and imported at routes/mcp.js:11.

writeRole.test.js contains the test 'a viewer connector is refused every write tool, and the graph is untouched', which drives every write tool as a viewer and asserts `isError` plus a `NOT_WORKSPACE_EDITOR` message.
Same claim as finding 3 (MCP write tools untested for a viewer), and likewise untrue — the MCP describe block covers viewer refusals, viewer reads, an editor write and a role-less membership.

triageGrades.reason: The change is entirely authorization: a new role gate on every content router plus the MCP write path.
No secret handling changes; the only token in the diff is a fake bearer value inside the new test fixture.

Right that money is touched — `POST /drafts` spends the workspace AI allowance and is now gated ahead of `checkBudget`, with `aiBudget.spentMicros` asserted unmoved (evidence pointer is the wrong file, which does not affect the verdict).
No deletions, migrations or data rewrites; DELETE routes are only gated, not changed.
No outbound third-party calls are added or changed; the MCP surface is this server's own endpoint.
No version bump, deploy config, env requirement or migration step in the diff.

summary: A poor review: all four findings are false — three assert gaps (MCP ungated, MCP write tools untested) that this very diff closes, and one claims a symbol is undefined that is defined in the diff — while the triage is entirely correct and the one real residual bypass (viewer writes via `POST /chat` relaying to the MCP server) was missed.
